All five Hurwitz minors independently factor as 12-6q, -2P3(q), -16P5(q), -192qS(q), -313344q^3 S(q). Q(0)=1632q^2>0 ensures simple symmetry zero. At each endpoint Delta2,Delta3,a4,a5>0 and the Routh auxiliary quadratic gives a simple imaginary pair while a residual cubic is strictly Hurwitz. originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality attaches only to the exact two-threshold shape-preserving heterogeneous M=3 full-amplitude spectral classification. The original Zhao–Uchida polygon construction and conjugate mirror-isospectral argument are prior art. The published SCOPE triangle results concern either a fixed 7-13-17 heterogeneous geometry with reactive coupling varied at fixed real coupling, or an identical-growth equilateral splay with its distinct quadratic stability condition. Their theorems do not contain this 1-sqrt(2)-sqrt(3) geometry, coupling C=q+4iq, compensating beta_j=j+3q, or an implication that yields these two sextic threshold crossings. The universal noncollinear attraction theorem treats purely reactive coupling and perturbatively small positive dissipation; it does not establish this complete dissipative-to-reactive ratio-4 path.
residual_risks: A historical general full-complex-coupling finite-rank spectrum classification could imply this polynomial after substitution; no exhaustive specialty-literature search was possible.

The choice beta_j=j+3q compensates coupling to freeze side lengths and is a deliberately one-dimensional exact slice; its relevance is the two-transition mechanism, not generic behavior for all heterogeneous populations.
The primary paper supplies underlying polygon existence and reflection isospectrality; no novelty is credited for those components.
Published phase-reduction literature and all pre-2026 global-coupling papers were not uniformly inspected in full.

value.rationale: The minimal nondegenerate zero-mean polygon in a full-amplitude heterogeneous network permits two chirality states. An exact all-positive-q bounded stability window, with loss–gain–loss via an algebraic pair-crossing boundary and full six-real-dimensional transverse criterion, resolves a naturally motivated question left open by numerical M=8 polygon maps. The growth-rate shift holds the geometry fixed, isolating coupling-induced stabilization from shape variation. The two distinct thresholds are nontrivial compared with the earlier single-threshold or purely reactive results; the exact fact can guide small-network bifurcation analysis even without a broad universality theorem.

final_claim: For beta_j=j+3q, C=q+4iq, omega=1, unit saturation and q>0, the two nondegenerate zero-mean triangles (1, +/- i sqrt(2), -1 -/+ i sqrt(2)) have exactly one symmetry zero and five stable transverse exponents iff the sharp sextic S(q) is negative, equivalently 0.1400529264...<q<0.5858841911...; at both boundary roots one additional simple pure-imaginary pair occurs; only local orbital exponential stability is claimed.
limitations: Local stability only; no global attractor census or nonlinear endpoint bifurcation classification.
